Director

Conversation No. 01  ·  The Director 07

Joel
Burke

Co-founder · Artistic Director · Choreographer

Joel Burke is an Australian choreographer, producer, dancer, director, and the co-founder of BIG Live. He began his dance training at the age of three and went on to become the first dancer to represent Queensland Ballet Academy at the prestigious Prix de Lausanne in Switzerland.

Following his return to Australia, Burke became acutely aware of the limited professional pathways available to emerging dancers. Rather than accept these constraints, he and Khalid Tarabay established BIG Live, with a vision to create new opportunities and expand the reach of ballet internationally.

Dracula is not a story about monstrosity. It is a story about a body that refuses to be finished. — J.B., rehearsal · 14.08.26

Burke's first full-length ballet, The Nutcracker, marked the beginning of a series of commercially successful productions, including Romeo and Juliet, Dracula, The Great Gatsby and Christmas Spectacular. In recent years, his works have become among the most widely attended ballets in Australia by an Australian choreographer. Under his artistic direction, BIG Live continues to tour extensively, with performances across Australia, UK, USA and Asia.

As resident choreographer of BIG Live, Burke creates exclusively for the company, developing a repertoire defined by strong musicality, theatricality, and a clear emphasis on narrative. His work is distinguished by its accessibility and its appeal to broad audiences, while maintaining a foundation in classical technique.

Burke remains closely involved in all aspects of the company's operations, from artistic creation and rehearsal direction to touring strategy, venue engagement, and marketing. Through BIG Live, he continues to advocate for a more inclusive and commercially viable future for ballet.

Conversation No. 02  ·  The Producer 09

Khalid
Tarabay

Co-founder · Executive Director

Khalid Tarabay is an entertainment lawyer, producer, and founder of BIG Live, where he leads the company's strategic direction, cultivates partnerships, and oversees touring and audience development. Born in Glasgow, Scotland, Khalid brings an international perspective shaped by a career spanning the live entertainment, music, and film industries.

A ballet company is, at heart, a slow promise: that what is made tonight is worth the bodies, the buildings, the years. — K.T., 2026

For over a decade, Khalid has advised artists, producers, and entertainment companies on intellectual property, international touring, deal structuring, and rights management. This expertise underpins BIG Live's model — delivering commercially viable, audience-focused productions that create stable, long-term employment for Australian performers without relying on government funding.

BIG Live was founded on the belief that ballet should be open and inclusive. The company's vision is to challenge public perceptions by presenting work that is visceral and authentic, respectful of tradition while adapting to contemporary audiences. Khalid is committed to removing barriers that have historically kept ballet behind closed doors.

Job creation is central to Khalid's mission for BIG Live, which offers rare, long-term roles for Australian dancers. These positions give local artists the chance to work with leading international performers, gain world-class experience, and build careers that strengthen the arts sector.

Synopsis · Act I
The Story 10

ACT
I

Damnation

Sc. 1
The Battlefield.   The 1600s. Vlad defeats an army of enemies. Victory turns bitter when a letter arrives: his beloved wife has been condemned and killed by the Church he served. Consumed by rage, he sells his soul and begins his transformation into Dracula, Lord of the Vampires.
Sc. 2
The Wedding.   Two centuries later. Joy fills the air at Jonathan and Mina's wedding. A honeymoon gift: a trip to Transylvania, doubling as a business venture to secure a deal with the mysterious Count.
Sc. 3
The Castle.   Night falls. Ghostly servants torment the couple. Jonathan is locked away; Mina is drawn to Dracula. Upon seeing her face, he falters — she is the image of his lost wife. Burning with jealousy, he transforms Jonathan into a vampire.
Synopsis · Act I 1 h 02 min · interval to follow
Synopsis · Act II
Big Live · Programme № 14
The Story · cont. 11

ACT
II

The Reckoning

Sc. 4
The Ghosts.   The ghosts appear — women who fell victim to the Count's power. Dracula commands them to leave until only Mina remains. Convinced she is his beloved returned, he lavishes devotion upon her. She recoils. The ghosts intervene.
Sc. 5
The Forest.   Jonathan battles his monstrous transformation. The ghosts deliver Mina into his arms. He fights desperately to resist — but the hunger wins. He kills the woman he loves.
Sc. 6
The Village.   Jonathan presents Mina's corpse. The villagers vow vengeance and storm Dracula's castle. Their courage is no match for his immortal power. The invasion becomes a massacre.
Sc. 7
Sacrifice.   Mina's ghost intervenes — dousing both men with holy water. With a stake, she pierces their hearts. Freed at last, yet unable to bear what she has done, Mina drives the stake into her own heart. The darkness is extinguished — and so is she.
Synopsis · Act II 53 min · no interval

Creators · I/II
Notes 12

Notes from the Creators.

Joel Burke
Artistic Director

When I first began imagining Dracula as a ballet, it was the story's enduring commercial power that caught my attention. For over a century, this tale has been retold, reshaped, and reinvented, and yet audiences still cannot resist its dark allure. I knew the physicality of the vampire — his dominance, menace, and seduction — would translate brilliantly into movement. Dracula was a story begging to be danced.

While Bram Stoker's novel served as the foundation, any staging of Dracula requires reinvention. Ballet demands clarity: a story distilled so audiences can follow every gesture and phrase without words. At its heart, this production explores a paradox. Even the most evil figures can be empathised with, and even the most virtuous may commit acts of darkness. Ballet, in its rawest form, is not only beauty and elegance but also something gory, primal, and human.

The movement language reflects that philosophy. Dracula himself is powerful and unapologetically masculine, a physicality rarely seen in ballet today. Jonathan also embodies strength, which curdles into a beast-like quality once transformed. Mina balances these forces, embodying both purity and sensuality.

Music sits at the very centre of Dracula. Working with composers Jason Fernandez and Toby Alexander, alongside a tapestry of classical works, we wove together a score that drives the story's gothic pulse. From the grandeur of the 1812 Overture to the haunting strains of Isle of the Dead and the delicacy of Clair de Lune, the score is both familiar and surprising.

The making of Dracula was intense: a five-month creation period in which the dancers themselves became co-authors. Their instincts and artistry shaped the movement, from the nine-minute pas de deux between Mina and Dracula in Act II — one of the most demanding sequences I have ever created — to the explosive, unpredictable finale set to the 1812 Overture.

For me, Dracula is not a metaphor, nor a moral fable. It is simply a great story told through ballet. Bold, visceral, and uncompromising.

Steven May
Lighting Design

The lighting design swings between two extremes: hyperreal and dramatic for the supernatural, then a watercolour-version of realism for the human stories. We incorporate motifs in colour and texture to correspond to characters and their relationships. As an artist I'm focused on lighting as a fundamentally interactive artform with the performers onstage, with the light-body interaction being the most important element — heavy focus on low sidelight and high sides, a very useful and powerful choice for dance works.

Jason Fernandez
Composer

Jason Fernandez is musical glue — an ultimate collaborator who does anything and everything musical to help tell the story. He has composed for Universal, Netflix, Warner Bros., and more, and shaped the music of The Beatles and Motown for Netflix, where the team won an Emmy. A trusted music technologist and producer, Jason has contributed to the music teams of A-list Hollywood composers like John Powell and Oscar nominee David Hirschfelder. He recently wrote the score for And Mrs. directed by Daniel Reisinger, which received great reviews.

The Antagonist  ·  The Count 13
A figure from the long dark

Dracula

ImmortalEnigmaticInsatiable

The immortal Lord of the Vampires and the tragic architect of his own demise. Once a devoted 17th-century warrior, he sold his soul after the Church unjustly murdered his beloved wife.

Characterised by ruthless cruelty and blinding obsession, Dracula retreats behind supernatural dominance to mask his enduring heartbreak.

When he encounters Mina — the exact image of his lost bride — his dormant grief twists into possessive fury.

Driven by jealous delusion, he turns her husband into a vampire, inadvertently causing Mina's death.

Ultimately, Dracula is a tragic figure who chooses destructive obsession over acceptance, leading to his ruin.

The Witness  ·  The Solicitor 15
An ordinary man, unrecovered

Jonathan Harker

EarnestUnpreparedAltered

An earnest newlywed whose naive pursuit of success leads him directly into the jaws of damnation. He represents the fragile nature of human resolve when faced with overwhelming evil.

Characterised by a desperate, failing struggle against his own corruption. Transformed into a vampire out of Dracula's petty jealousy, Jonathan is tormented by a monstrous hunger he cannot control.

His arc is not toward heroism, but toward ruin — the slow unravelling of everything he once believed himself to be.

By succumbing to his cursed nature and killing his beloved Mina, Jonathan demonstrates how easily purity can be twisted into unspeakable ruin.

Ultimately, he is a broken, tragic figure who becomes the instrument of his own despair.

Character Profile · III/IV
Big Live · Programme № 14
The Centre  ·  The Storyteller 17
The Centre Holds

Mina Harker

LucidDevotedUnafraid

The innocent bride whose uncanny resemblance to Dracula's deceased wife unwittingly positions her at the centre of a centuries-old tragedy. Characterised by a fierce inner strength that defies her initial victimisation.

Though she is tragically murdered by her cursed husband, death does not silence her. She bravely refuses to be reduced to a mere replacement for a dead woman.

Ultimately, she evolves from a helpless pawn into the story's resolute saviour.

Returning as a merciful spirit, Mina sacrifices herself entirely — destroying the monsters and severing her own tether to the earth.

If the work has a moral, Mina carries it: that to reclaim stolen peace, one must be willing to give everything.

Character Profile · IV/IV
Big Live · Programme № 14
The Chorus  ·  What Remains 19
Neither alive, nor finished

The Ghosts

MemoryMultitudeRefusal

The spectral remnants of Dracula's past victims, serving as both instruments of his malice and the suppressed conscience of his castle. Once women of flesh and breath, now neither living nor truly dead.

When Jonathan and Mina arrive at the castle, it is the Ghosts who appear in the dark to torment them, separating the newlyweds and drawing Mina toward their master through a strange, dreamlike spell.

Yet beneath their menace flickers something more complicated. Having suffered at Dracula's hand themselves, they recognise Mina's terror.

When his fury threatens to consume her, it is the Ghosts who intervene, urging him to release her.

Bound to obey, yet quietly mournful, they are Dracula's chorus and his conscience: a haunting reminder of every life he has taken, and of the cost of the curse he chose.

Principal Artist 20

Ervin Zagidullan

Principal

As Count Dracula  ·  opening night, 14 Oct

Born in Kazan (2000) and a Vaganova Academy graduate (2018), Ervin won prizes at the Vaganova-Prix and Istanbul (2024) and was a Finalist in Prix de Lausanne. After performing at the Mariinsky Theatre and Ankara State Ballet, he joined BIG Live in 2024. His 2025 season features leading roles including Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, the title role in Dracula, and the Prince in The Nutcracker. He performed Diana & Acteon in Ballet International Gala VI with Abbey Hansen.

Principal Artist 21

Abbey Hansen

Principal

As Mina Harker  ·  opening night, 14 Oct

Born in Brisbane (2002), Abbey began ballet training at the age of 8 before being accepted into The Australian Ballet School, where she trained for three years. She returned to Brisbane to join BIG Live, touring nationally with every Ballet International Gala series. Her leading roles include Mina in Dracula and Sugar Plum Fairy in The Nutcracker (2023 and 2024). She danced alongside Daniil Simkin during the 2023 Nutcracker season at Melbourne's Hamer Hall.

About

24 · About biglive.com
About
Big Live · Programme № 14
Founded MMXIX · Sydney · London 25
World-class ballet · extraordinary scale

The Southern Hemisphere's fastest-growing international ballet company.

BIG Live redefines the classical experience, bringing world-class, large-scale productions to the world's most prestigious theatres across Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Driven by the belief that ballet should be relevant and widely accessible, we present story-led works grounded in rigorous classical technique but delivered with a contemporary theatrical energy.

From the dark romanticism of Dracula and the glamour of The Great Gatsby to the enduring magic of The Nutcracker, our productions ensure emotional clarity and genuine spectacle.

We unite internationally renowned principal artists with a purpose-built ensemble selected specifically for their strength, stamina and stage presence.

Beyond our touring productions, we are the force behind the Ballet International Gala (BIG) — the largest event of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere.

Wherever it performs, BIG Live remains focused on one principle: world-class ballet presented through extraordinary artists, compelling storytelling, and exceptional scale.
